knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = TRUE)

Work through this file alongside the chapter "Spread and Standard Error" in the book. Keep it in the same folder as your `my_functions.R`.

## The data

```{r data}
x <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
```

## Load your toolbox

```{r load-toolbox}
library(tidyverse)
source("my_functions.R")

all.equal(my_mean(x), mean(x))
all.equal(my_var(x), var(x))
```

You are looking for two `TRUE`s. If you see `could not find function`, finish the toolbox section at the end of the "From Equations to Code" exercise file first.

## Your turn: write `my_sd()`

```{r my-sd}

}

my_sd(x)
```

### Check it against `sd()`

```{r my-sd-check}
c(mine = my_sd(x), R = sd(x))
all.equal(my_sd(x), sd(x))
```

```{r my-sd-check-2}
c(mine = my_sd(c(2, 4, 9)), R = sd(c(2, 4, 9)))
all.equal(my_sd(c(2, 4, 9)), sd(c(2, 4, 9)))
```

## Seeing standard error

A population of scores, then one sample of 20. Run the second chunk a few times.

```{r population}
population_scores <- rnorm(n = 10000, mean = 50, sd = 10)
my_mean(population_scores)
my_sd(population_scores)
```

```{r one-sample}
one_sample <- sample(population_scores, size = 20)
my_mean(one_sample)
```

Repeat that 1000 times and compare the spread of the sample means with the formula.

```{r many-samples}
one_sample_mean <- function(n) {
  one_sample <- sample(population_scores, size = n)
  my_mean(one_sample)
}

sample_means_20 <- replicate(1000, one_sample_mean(n = 20))

c(
  simulated = my_sd(sample_means_20),
  formula = my_sd(population_scores) / sqrt(20)
)
```

Try changing 20 to 5 and then 50 in both places. What happens to the standard error?

## Your turn: write `my_summary()`

Fill in each column. Use your own functions wherever you can.

```{r my-summary}
my_summary <- function(x) {
  output <- tibble(
    n = ,
    mean = ,
    variance = ,
    sd = ,
    se =
  )
  return(output)
}

my_summary(x)
```

### Check it against R

```{r my-summary-check}
r_summary <- tibble(
  n = length(x),
  mean = mean(x),
  variance = var(x),
  sd = sd(x),
  se = t.test(x)$stderr
)

bind_rows(mine = my_summary(x), R = r_summary, .id = "version")
all.equal(my_summary(x), r_summary)
```

```{r my-z-score-check}
tibble(value = x, mine = my_z_score(x), R = as.vector(scale(x)))

```

## Try it on real data

`sleep` is a dataset built into R: 10 patients who each tried two sleeping drugs. `extra` is how many more hours they slept on a drug, and `group` says which drug. This picks out the extra sleep for the first drug:

```{r real-data}
drug_1 <- sleep %>% filter(group == 1) %>% pull(extra)
drug_1

all.equal(my_sd(drug_1), sd(drug_1))
all.equal(my_se(drug_1), t.test(drug_1)$stderr)
all.equal(my_z_score(drug_1), as.vector(scale(drug_1)))
```

## Add to your toolbox

1. Open `my_functions.R`.
2. Copy your finished `my_sd()`, `my_se()`, `my_summary()`, and `my_z_score()` into it, under the **Spread and Standard Error** heading. Copy only the functions.
3. Save `my_functions.R`.

Now check that the saved toolbox works on its own. The first line clears your environment, so the functions can only come from your file. You are looking for six `TRUE`s.

```{r toolbox-check}
rm(list = ls())
source("my_functions.R")

values <- c(2, 4, 9)
all.equal(my_mean(values), mean(values))
all.equal(my_var(values), var(values))
all.equal(my_sd(values), sd(values))
all.equal(my_se(values), t.test(values)$stderr)
all.equal(my_summary(values)$se, t.test(values)$stderr)
all.equal(my_z_score(values), as.vector(scale(values)))
```

If you see `could not find function`, that function is not in `my_functions.R` yet, or the file was not saved.
